Saraswati – Igniting Hope Through Education
Maa Saraswati – mother of all knowledge – is the divine name of the Supreme for seekers of Vidya.

In India, while education is fundamentally a birthright, it tragically remains an elusive luxury for countless children trapped in the harsh realities of impoverished slum communities. Here, the immediate struggle for survival often eclipses the pursuit of knowledge, diverting young lives from the path of learning. The Jan Swabhiman Welfare Society's Saraswati initiative stands as a beacon of hope, passionately dedicated to transforming this stark reality by providing free, holistic education to these underprivileged children.
Our Comprehensive Approach: Nurturing Minds, Body, and Soul
Saraswati is far more than a conventional education
emotion that fuels our teams

, driving us to ensure the comprehensive growth and development of these young minds who were previously denied their birthright – the opportunity to bloom and transcend the societal barriers of caste and creed.
We operate directly within the heart of slum areas, including specialized centers dedicated to children from Pakistani Hindu refugee camps.

This ensures we directly address the critical educational needs of those most affected by extreme poverty, social challenges, and adverse environments. Our thoughtfully designed program is built to foster both academic excellence and profound personal well-being.
Key Pillars of Our Program:
Free & Accessible Education (6 Days a Week):

We're committed to breaking down financial barriers, ensuring quality education is absolutely free and accessible to every child. We hold daily classes, six days a week, so no cost ever prevents a child from learning and growing.
Essential Learning Resources:
To empower every student, we provide all necessary tools for learning, including
free books, notebooks, and stationery.

In a world where digital literacy is essential, we introduce children to computers through guided sessions — basic skills, confidence at the keyboard, and the curiosity to explore tools they may never otherwise encounter at home.
Holistic Personal Development:
Our curriculum extends significantly beyond traditional academics. Each day begins with the
spiritual chants from the Vedas
, promoting mental clarity and spiritual harmony. Regular
sessions are integral, instilling strong moral values, celebrating the richness of Indian culture, sharing ancient Vedic wisdom, and exploring our glorious history. There's a strong emphasis on
to nurture compassionate and
Family and Child Counseling:
Recognizing the importance of a supportive home environment, we offer frequent, personalized
for both children and their families, fostering conditions conducive to learning and healthy growth.
Health and Well-being Support:
We prioritize the overall health of our students. Occasional visits from qualified doctors provide vital
health counseling, comprehensive check-ups, and free medicines
, directly addressing critical health needs within the community.
Sports & Physical Activity:
We make room for play and sport so children build strength, teamwork, and joy alongside their studies — healthy bodies supporting focused minds, and friendships formed beyond the classroom.
Vibrant Cultural Enrichment:
Beyond traditional academics, Saraswati meticulously cultivates
a vibrant, positive, and truly inclusive environment.
Our centers come alive during
cultural events and festivals
, where kids delight in refreshments, the excitement of bursting crackers, the joy of playing with colors, and simply the freedom to have fun.
Breaking Barriers & Expanding Our Reach
Crucially, Saraswati is also a dedicated and unwavering effort to
dismantle societal barriers of caste and creed.
We are actively building a future where
every single child has an equal opportunity to learn, thrive, and realize their full potential, irrespective of their background.
multiple centers across Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, and Delhi NCR
, dedicated to providing free education to children from Pakistani Hindu refugee families, as well as urban slums and ragpicker communities.
benefiting approximately 2000 children
, including over 1500 Pakistani Hindu refugee kids.
The Power of VidyaDaan: Nurturing Futures

We firmly believe that VidyaDaan (the gift of knowledge) is the most profound of all donations, for knowledge imparted at an early age fundamentally guides and builds a child's career and character. Many of the children we serve lack anyone to look after their basic educational needs. Their parents, struggling with daily necessities, find educating their children an insurmountable challenge. Our dedicated volunteers step in to fill this critical educational void, providing support to the greatest extent possible.
From Darkness to Light: The Saraswati Transformation
Cultivating Values & Pride:

Through our efforts, these kids aren't just gaining an education; they're actively training to become educated patriots, instilled with a profound pride in India's glorious culture. This instills a sense of spirituality, discipline, respect, and responsibility, preparing them to become good human beings and contribute meaningfully to the nation's future.
The behavioral changes we've observed in our students are remarkable. Children who previously struggled with basic communication, often resorting to abusive language, have genuinely transformed.
From Disruptive to Dedicated:
They've blossomed into tiny, bright souls passionately pursuing knowledge, showcasing a newfound focus and enthusiasm for learning.
Special Support For Our Pakistani Hindu Refugee Children
We operate dedicated centers for Hindu children who have migrated from Pakistan and are living in refugee camps across India. These centers are managed in collaboration with
, a remarkable team of Pakistani Hindu refugees in India led by Dr. Vashi Sharma (an IIT-Scientist and our mentor).
These children fled Pakistan due to extreme persecution, abductions, and forced conversions.
With the twin pillars of education and protection, we are nurturing them to become the scientists, engineers, entrepreneurs, sportspersons, and social activists of tomorrow.

story.challenge: In the urban slums and refugee settlements of Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, and Delhi NCR, generations of children were trapped in cyclical poverty, child labour, and neglect. For many, even acquiring a single notebook or clean pencil was an insurmountable hurdle.
story.action: Jan Swabhiman established full-time, 6-day-a-week Saraswati Learning Centers right in the heart of these settlements. Run by dedicated educationists and volunteers, our centers provide not just textbooks, but nutritional meals, doctor checkups, digital computer labs, and daily Vedic recitations.
story.impact: Children once vulnerable to exploitation have blossomed into confident, bright minds dreaming of becoming scientists, teachers, and national leaders. Disruptive language has given way to Sanskrit mantras, mutual respect, and academic distinction.

O Divine Mother of Knowledge,
You are Varadā – the fulfiller of noble desires.
You are Veda Mata – the eternal source of wisdom.
You are Pāvamānī – the purifier of mind and soul.
Bestowed upon the devoted, carried forward by the wise,
You grant us life, strength, prosperity, and light.
Not just sacred sound – You are Matrishakti in radiant form, guiding souls, awakening truth, and nurturing the rise of dharma.
When She Rises, the Nation Awakens

– the divine feminine force – not merely as a symbol of care, but as the source of courage, leadership, and transformation. Empowering

story.challenge: Across the border in Pakistan, minority Hindu families endure unspeakable religious persecution, forced conversions of young daughters, blasphemy accusations, and complete institutional erasure. , we believe that Dharma begins where compassion is practiced — not just for humans, but for all living beings. Our Animal Welfare and Gau Seva initiatives are grounded in the sacred ethos of
We serve the voiceless — those who cannot ask for help, but feel pain, hunger, fear, and love just like we do.
The cow is more than an animal — she is Gaumata, the gentle nurturer, the symbol of abundance and purity, and the sacred heartbeat of our cultural identity.

Many gausevaks work with us on this mission, and we support them financially. It's risky work — some are injured in the course of a rescue — and when that happens, we take full responsibility for their families and medical treatment.
Our Gau Seva work includes:
Rescuing injured, abandoned, or abused cows from roads, gutters, and slaughter-bound transport
Medical treatment and recovery care through on-site clinics and mobile first-aid vans
Daily feeding (Gau Graas) and long-term shelter for rescued Gaumatas
For the Gaumatas we could not save, we perform Antim Sanskaar (last rites) with dignity.
Gau Raksha is Rashtra Raksha.
Serving the cow is serving the nation, its soil, and its soul.

We support genuine Gaushalas on a need basis with financial assistance for gaugraas (cow feed), medicines, and more. We regularly support Shri Krishna Arjun Gaushala at Noida for monthly gaugraas and medicines. The Noida Gaushala shelters 100+ cows. Many arrived after being abandoned due to old age or illness, rescued from roadside accidents, gutters, or illegal slaughter routes, or left behind after being considered “unproductive” by previous owners.

fullText: Gaushala – A Sanctuary of Love, Service, and Dharma
Gaushala – A Sanctuary Of Love, Service, And Dharma

At Jan Swabhiman, we believe that Gaumata is not just an animal — she is our cultural mother, our ecological guardian, and a sacred being worthy of love, protection, and reverence. Our Gaushala in Noida is a living embodiment of this belief — a space where compassion meets commitment, and service becomes sacred.
Located In Noida – Home To Over 100 Rescued Gaumatas
Our Gaushala currently shelters 100+ cows, many of whom were:
Abandoned due to old age or illness
Rescued from roadside accidents, gutters, or illegal slaughter routes
Left to die after being considered “unproductive” by their owners
Here, each Gaumata is welcomed with warmth — fed, healed, and given a peaceful space to live out her years with dignity.
₹5,100 / $61 = GAU GRAAS FOR ONE GAUMATA FOR ONE MONTH
₹21,000 / $251 = GAU GRAAS FOR ALL 100+ GAUMATAS FOR ONE DAY
Daily Gauseva – Compassion In Action
Gauseva is our daily ritual. With the help of volunteers, caretakers, and donors, we ensure:
Two daily meals of fresh fodder, wheat bran, and jaggery
Constant supply of clean water and shaded resting areas
On-site medical care: dressing of wounds, parasite treatment, and vet visits
Regular Gau Pujan and prayer sessions, connecting community and cows in spiritual oneness
Each cow is not a burden — she is a blessing. And each day of care is a tribute to Bharat's dharmic tradition.
Protecting indigenous breeds
Nurturing natural agriculture through Panchagavya
Restoring ecological balance
Preserving Dharma through service to a being revered in every scripture of Bharat
A Gaushala is not a shelter. It is a temple of silent blessings, where compassion meets culture.
₹5,100 / $61 = GAU GRAAS FOR ONE GAUMATA FOR ONE MONTH
₹21,000 / $251 = GAU GRAAS FOR ALL 100+ GAUMATAS FOR ONE DAY
Gauseva is Gau Raksha. Gau Raksha is Rashtra Raksha.
In serving Gaumata, we serve our ancestors, our soil, our soul.
Join us in this sacred duty. Let no cow suffer alone. Let every cow live with love.

Tribal Welfare – Preserving Identity, Restoring Dignity

Across remote forested regions and hilly terrains, tribal communities — rich in indigenous wisdom and dharmic heritage — have often been left behind in the race of development. Deprived of basic amenities and guidance, many families fall prey to animal trafficking, drug addiction, and illegal conversion rackets.
To address these deep-rooted challenges, Jan Swabhiman Welfare Society runs a holistic Tribal Welfare Program, grounded in

Dang, Tapi, Valsad, Navsari
These are regions where our teams live among the people, understand their concerns firsthand, and work shoulder to shoulder to create lasting change.
Rozgar Vyavastha – Self Employment for Poor Tribal Men and Women
We help tribal men and women build livelihoods through machines and small units — for example paper plate making machines. Women can earn around ₹15,000 per month. One machine supports four families.
Ways to support: Sponsor a machine · Sponsor self-employment for 5 families.
Supporting Orphan and Poor Children
We support orphans, children from broken families, and extremely poor children.
Clothing Distribution for the Needy
Through regular Clothes Seva Drives, our volunteers distribute clean and season-appropriate clothes to poor tribal families — especially during winters, monsoons, and festivals.
Free Food for Hospital Patients
In government and rural hospitals, tribal families often go hungry while tending to the sick. We provide hot, nutritious meals free of cost to tribal patients and their caregivers.
Youth Fitness and Sports Engagement

To channel the energy of tribal youth away from addiction and idleness, we host sports tournaments (kabaddi, kho-kho, and more) and village-level fitness and physical training — building confidence, resilience, and team spirit.
Sanskritic Punarjagran (Cultural Reclamation)

In the absence of proper social guidance, tribal youth fall victim to animal trafficking, drug addiction, and illegal conversion rackets. Families form and break without marriage, and children from such families are left clueless.

Tribal values are rooted in ancient Vedic values. Through Tulsi Poojan, poojan of Shabari Mata, tribal cultural traditions, and remembrance of tribal heroes such as Birsa Munda, we evoke reverence and self-respect.
Village-level events draw a crowd of 400–500 people. Programmes include Agnihotra, Kanya Poojan, Bhajan Keertan, and Prasad Vitaran.

Standing with Communities in Crisis
This page looks back at past relief missions. It is not an active programme page.

, we have stood with communities in moments of crisis — floods, pandemic hardship, and drought — with food, care, and hands-on help. The missions below are part of our record of seva. We share them so the work is remembered, not as a call for an ongoing relief vertical.
During flood seasons in Assam, our teams reached affected communities with ration kits, medical support, and on-ground volunteers — standing with families when waters rose and homes were cut off.
When floods hit Uttar Pradesh, our teams also took part in cow rescue — helping Gaumatas and animals stranded or endangered by rising waters, alongside support for affected communities.
Through the pandemic years, Jan Swabhiman carried out Covid relief — reaching families and communities under lockdown and hardship with essential support when need was acute.

In 2019, drought struck Barmer, Rajasthan, and thousands of cows faced death from lack of fodder and water. We ran a 22-day relief campaign, saving more than 8,000 cows across Barmer and nearby districts.
Relief Work is not an active programme line right now. If you wish to support Jan Swabhiman's ongoing seva, you can give here or through our CSR partnerships.
